02 / 16ARCHITECTURE

Encryption:
Olm & Megolm

ONE-TO-ONE

Olm

Double Ratchet

A compromised current key does not reveal earlier messages.

GROUP CONVERSATIONS

Megolm

One key per session

A shared session key is reused until rotation. Compromise puts later messages in that session at risk.

↳
Key backupOptional server backup, encrypted with a separate passphrase.

07 / 16COMPARISON

A typology
of criminal users

Drug-trafficking networks

After EncroChat and Sky ECC: interest in self-managed tools. Mass migration to Matrix is not confirmed.

Ransomware groups

Jabber / XMPP remains the main channel. Matrix runs in parallel for specific tasks.

Extremist communities

Documented cases are isolated. Other platforms include Telegram and RocketChat.

Financial fraud networks

Laundering, carding and BEC. Far fewer documented Matrix cases than Telegram or forum cases.

12 / 16SECURITY LAYERS

Server seizure:
what investigators can see

What is present

  • Matrix IDs, password hashes, account dates
  • Login IPs and User-Agents
  • Room events, timestamps and senders
  • Ciphertext and federation logs

What is missing

Readable content without device keys.
Phone / email if never supplied.

OTHER VECTORS

Unlocked devices · nickname OSINT · room infiltration

13 / 16EVIDENCE

EU Chat Control:
three setbacks and a trilogue

2022

Initial European Commission proposal

2023

“Don’t Scan Us”: 1.1M signatures. Signal, Threema and Element oppose CSS.

09.2025

Blocked a third time: Germany and Luxembourg

11.2025

New wording: “risk mitigation”

19.11.2025

Council position: no mandatory scanning; voluntary scanning allowed

03.04.2026

Temporary Regulation EU 2021/1232 expires

09.2026

Trilogue; Parliament’s version excludes E2E

THE PROPOSAL

Scan content for CSAM before encryption.

Barriers for Matrix

No single operator.

Open code allows a client without CSS.

Homeservers span multiple jurisdictions.

14 / 16REGULATION

The future of
criminal communications

01

Multiple migration paths

Drug networks switch commercial products. Ransomware keeps Jabber, with Matrix in parallel.

02

People remain vulnerable

No case presented involves breaking Olm or Megolm.

03

Control has limits

Devices, infiltration, OSINT and operator mistakes remain practical routes.
